metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened Chrome, navigated to google.com/preferences (Google Search Settings), scrolled through settings, clicked 'Other settings', but couldn't find the 'Results per page' setting. Failed after 50 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open Chrome, navigate URLs via address bar (type + Enter), scroll web pages, and reach google.com/preferences.
metadata.failure_analysis: The modern Google Search Settings UI no longer exposes a 'Results per page' slider. The agent spent all turns searching for a setting that no longer exists in the current Google interface.
metadata.task_rationale: Simplify from failed rollout: target the stable prefix action (navigating to google.com/preferences) as the full task. URL-based evaluator is robust and negative-control resistant (desktop initial state has no browser URL).
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening Chrome and navigating to the Google Search Settings page at google.com/preferences. Evaluator uses active_url_from_accessTree to read the current active tab URL and checks it matches the google.com/preferences pattern. Initial desktop state (no browser) does not pass.

llm_judge_reasons: The getter (active_url_from_accessTree) correctly reads the Chrome address bar from the accessibility tree and prepends 'https://www.' to form the active URL — appropriate for this navigation task.

The metric (is_expected_url_pattern_match) receives the rules dict directly (since expected.type='rule'), and correctly accesses rules['expected'] to get the regex patterns — no parameter-handling bug.
The regex pattern 'google\.com/preferences' is matched via re.search against the constructed URL, which correctly verifies that the Google Search Settings page is open.
Single instruction requirement (open google.com/preferences in Chrome) is fully covered by the evaluator.
Negative-control resistant: initial desktop state has no Chrome browser open, so the getter returns None and the metric returns 0.0.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The goto_prefix 'https://www.' combined with an address bar showing 'www.google.com/preferences' would produce a doubled 'www.' in the URL ('https://www.www.google.com/preferences'). This does not break verification since re.search is used, but using goto_prefix 'https://' would be cleaner.
